Any two of these are usually enough to stay upright on a narrow base, so a person who has lost proprioception quietly leans on vision instead. Closing the eyes removes that substitute, and sway grows until the patient must step or would fall. Cerebellar ataxia is a failure of coordinating the output rather than of sensing position, so it is present with eyes open and changes comparatively little when vision is removed.
det.technique: Ask the patient to stand with feet together, arms at the sides or folded, and first confirm they are steady with eyes open for about 30 seconds. Then ask them to close the eyes for up to 60 seconds while you stand close with arms ready, warning them beforehand that you will catch them. A positive result is loss of balance requiring a step, not merely a little increased sway. Harder versions — heel-to-toe (sharpened) Romberg or standing on a foam pad — increase sensitivity in mild neuropathy or vestibular loss but are often failed by healthy older adults.
det.interpretation: Stability with eyes open and loss of balance with eyes closed indicates sensory ataxia from large-fibre neuropathy, sensory ganglionopathy or dorsal column disease: B12 or copper deficiency, nitrous oxide misuse, tabes dorsalis, Friedreich ataxia, CIDP and anti-MAG neuropathy, or ganglionopathy from Sjögren syndrome, paraneoplastic anti-Hu disease, cisplatin or pyridoxine excess. Bilateral vestibular failure also gives a positive Romberg, and an acute unilateral vestibular lesion may cause a tendency to fall toward the affected side. If the patient cannot stand with feet together even with eyes open, the test cannot be interpreted and midline cerebellar or other disease is more likely. Dramatic sway from the hips that never results in a fall, or that settles when the patient is distracted, suggests a functional disorder.
pearls: Romberg tests the sensory inputs to balance, not cerebellar function.
The test is only valid if the patient is steady with eyes open.
Positive Romberg with absent ankle jerks and extensor plantars: think B12, copper, nitrous oxide or Friedreich ataxia.
Count a step or fall as positive; mild sway alone is normal.
det.thd: Romberg ทดสอบระบบรับความรู้สึกที่ช่วยการทรงตัว (proprioception และ vestibular) คนที่ proprioception จากขาเสียจะอาศัยสายตาทรงตัวแทน พอหลับตาจึงเซจนต้องก้าวเท้าหรือล้ม ตรวจโดยให้ยืนเท้าชิดลืมตาจนนิ่งก่อน แล้วหลับตาไม่เกิน 60 วินาทีโดยผู้ตรวจยืนประกบพร้อมรับ ผลบวกบ่งชี้ large-fibre neuropathy, ganglionopathy หรือ dorsal column เสีย เช่น B12 หรือทองแดงต่ำ ไนตรัสออกไซด์ tabes และ CIDP หรือ vestibular เสียสองข้าง ส่วนผู้ป่วยสมองน้อยจะเซตั้งแต่ลืมตาจึงแปลผลไม่ได้

name: Clonus
formal: Rhythmic involuntary muscle contractions provoked by sudden sustained stretch, most often at the ankle; more than a few beats indicates upper motor neuron hyperexcitability.
simple: When the foot is quickly pushed up and held, it keeps bouncing up and down by itself — a sign of an overactive reflex from brain or spinal cord damage.
th: ดันข้อเท้าขึ้นเร็ว ๆ แล้วค้างไว้ เท้ากระตุกเป็นจังหวะต่อเนื่อง — บ่งชี้ UMN lesion
exam: With the knee slightly flexed and supported, briskly dorsiflex the foot and hold gentle pressure.
pos: Sustained (>3–5 beats) = UMN lesion. A few unsustained beats may be normal with anxiety or brisk reflexes; serotonin toxicity gives inducible clonus too.
aN: ankle clonus | sustained clonus | patellar clonus

det.mechanism: Clonus is a self-sustaining oscillation in which each stretch evokes a reflex contraction that relaxes and re-stretches the muscle, triggering the next beat. It requires hyperexcitable stretch reflex circuits after loss of descending inhibition, and the beat frequency (around 5–7 Hz at the ankle) depends on the reflex loop time. It is the extreme end of hyperreflexia.
det.technique: Support the leg with the knee slightly flexed and the muscles relaxed. Dorsiflex the ankle briskly and maintain moderate upward pressure on the sole; count the beats. Patellar clonus is elicited by a sharp downward push of the patella with the knee extended. Tense, cold or poorly positioned limbs give false negatives.
det.interpretation: Sustained clonus (more than a few beats continuing while stretch is held) indicates an UMN lesion. A short unsustained run of beats can occur in anxious or healthy people, especially if symmetrical. Asymmetry is more significant than amplitude. Inducible and ocular clonus with hyperthermia and agitation suggest serotonin toxicity.
pearls: Count and record the number of beats.
Symmetrical non-sustained clonus may be normal.
det.thd: Clonus เกิดจากรีเฟล็กซ์ยืดที่ไวมากจนกระตุกต่อเนื่องเป็นรอบ ๆ เมื่อขาดการยับยั้งจากสมอง ตรวจโดยงอเข่าเล็กน้อยแล้วดันข้อเท้าขึ้นเร็ว ๆ ค้างไว้และนับจำนวนครั้ง ถ้ากระตุกต่อเนื่องมากกว่า 3–5 ครั้งบ่งชี้รอยโรค UMN แต่ถ้ากระตุกไม่กี่ครั้งสองข้างเท่ากันอาจเป็นปกติ และพบใน serotonin toxicity ได้

name: Kernig Sign
formal: Resistance or pain on extending the knee with the hip flexed to 90°, reflecting meningeal irritation.
simple: With the hip bent, straightening the knee causes pain and resistance in the back — a sign of inflamed coverings of the brain and spine.
th: งอสะโพก 90° แล้วเหยียดเข่าไม่ได้เพราะปวด — บ่งชี้เยื่อหุ้มสมองระคายเคือง
exam: Patient supine. Flex hip and knee to 90°, then try to extend the knee.
pos: Pain/resistance limiting extension = meningeal irritation (meningitis, SAH). Low sensitivity — a negative test does not exclude meningitis.
aN: kernig | meningism | meningeal sign

det.mechanism: Extending the knee while the hip is flexed stretches the sciatic nerve and lumbosacral roots through the subarachnoid space. If the meninges and roots are inflamed or irritated by blood, this stretch is painful, so the hamstrings contract protectively to limit extension.
det.technique: With the patient supine, flex the hip and knee to 90 degrees, then slowly extend the knee. Positive when pain in the back or posterior thigh and resistance prevent extension beyond about 135 degrees. Perform bilaterally; unilateral resistance suggests a root problem rather than meningitis.
det.interpretation: Specificity for meningitis is relatively high, but sensitivity is low (often well under 20% in adult series), so a negative result must never delay lumbar puncture when meningitis is suspected. Signs may be absent in infants, the elderly, immunosuppressed or comatose patients. Lumbar disc disease and hamstring tightness can mimic a positive test.
pearls: Low sensitivity — do not use to rule out meningitis.
Bilateral finding favours meningeal irritation; unilateral suggests radiculopathy.
det.thd: Kernig sign เกิดจากการเหยียดเข่าขณะงอสะโพกทำให้รากประสาทและเยื่อหุ้มที่อักเสบถูกยืด จึงปวดและเหยียดไม่ได้ ตรวจโดยงอสะโพกและเข่า 90 องศาแล้วค่อย ๆ เหยียดเข่า ความไวต่ำมาก ผลลบจึงไม่ตัดเยื่อหุ้มสมองอักเสบ ถ้าสงสัยยังต้องเจาะหลังหรือให้ยาตามข้อบ่งชี้

name: Brudzinski Neck Sign
formal: Involuntary flexion of hips and knees when the neck is passively flexed, indicating meningeal irritation.
simple: Bending the patient's head forward makes the knees and hips bend by themselves — a sign of meningitis or bleeding around the brain.
th: ก้มคอผู้ป่วยแล้วสะโพกเข่างอเอง — บ่งชี้เยื่อหุ้มสมองระคายเคือง
exam: Patient supine; place a hand behind the head and flex the neck toward the chest.
pos: Reflex hip/knee flexion = meningeal irritation; specific but insensitive.
aN: brudzinski | brudzinski sign

det.mechanism: Flexing the neck draws the spinal cord, dura and nerve roots upward within the canal, so the lumbosacral roots are stretched over their exit foramina. When the meninges and roots are inflamed by infection or irritated by subarachnoid blood, this traction is painful. Bending the hips and knees slackens the sciatic nerve and its roots, so the patient flexes the legs reflexively to relieve the tension. The sign is therefore a protective withdrawal from root stretch, closely related to Kernig sign and neck stiffness.
det.technique: Lay the patient flat and relaxed with legs extended. Put one hand behind the occiput and bring the chin toward the chest smoothly, keeping the other hand on the sternum so the trunk does not rise. A positive response is involuntary flexion of both hips and knees as the neck bends; record any associated pain or resistance. Do not perform it when cervical spine injury or instability is possible, and interpret it cautiously if the patient is agitated, in pain elsewhere or unable to relax.
det.interpretation: A positive sign supports meningeal irritation from bacterial, viral, tuberculous or fungal meningitis or subarachnoid haemorrhage. Its specificity is reasonably high, but sensitivity in adult series is low (often well below 20%), so a negative response must never delay lumbar puncture, imaging or empirical antibiotics when meningitis is suspected. Meningeal signs are frequently absent in infants, older adults, immunocompromised and deeply comatose patients, and early in the illness. Leg flexion may also reflect lumbar disc disease or hamstring tightness, and stiffness to neck flexion alone may come from cervical spondylosis or parkinsonian rigidity.
pearls: Like Kernig, a negative result never excludes meningitis.
Clinical suspicion, not meningeal signs, should drive the decision for LP and antibiotics.
Brudzinski's contralateral leg sign (flexing one hip makes the other flex) is a rarely used variant.
Jolt accentuation of headache is a quick added test in alert patients but is also imperfect.
det.thd: Brudzinski sign คือเมื่อก้มคอผู้ป่วยแล้วสะโพกและเข่างอเอง เพราะการก้มคอดึงไขสันหลังและรากประสาทที่อักเสบให้ยืด ผู้ป่วยจึงงอขาเพื่อลดแรงดึงและความปวด ตรวจในท่านอนหงายโดยประคองท้ายทอยก้มคอให้คางชิดอก อีกมือกดอกไว้ไม่ให้ลำตัวยกขึ้น และห้ามทำถ้าสงสัยกระดูกคอบาดเจ็บ ผลบวกสนับสนุนเยื่อหุ้มสมองอักเสบหรือ SAH แต่ความไวต่ำมาก โดยเฉพาะในทารก ผู้สูงอายุ ผู้ป่วยภูมิต่ำ หรือหมดสติ จึงห้ามใช้ผลลบเป็นเหตุให้ชะลอการเจาะหลังหรือให้ยาปฏิชีวนะ

name: Neck Stiffness
formal: Resistance to passive neck flexion with preserved rotation, a feature of meningeal irritation; global resistance in all directions suggests cervical spine disease or parkinsonian rigidity instead.
simple: The chin cannot be brought down to the chest because of pain and stiffness, though turning the head side to side is fine — typical of meningitis or bleeding.
th: คอแข็ง ก้มคอไม่ได้แต่หันซ้ายขวาได้ — บ่งชี้เยื่อหุ้มสมองระคายเคือง
exam: Patient lying flat; gently lift the head to flex the neck, then test rotation.
pos: Resistance to flexion only = meningeal irritation; may be absent in coma, infants, the elderly and early disease.
aN: nuchal rigidity | meningism | neck rigidity | meningismus

det.mechanism: Inflammation or blood in the subarachnoid space irritates the meninges and nerve roots; neck flexion stretches these structures, triggering protective spasm of the posterior neck muscles. Rotation stretches the meninges much less, so it is relatively preserved, unlike in bony or extrapyramidal stiffness.
det.technique: With the patient lying flat and the head on your hands, gently lift the head to bring the chin toward the chest, then rotate side to side. Resistance to flexion with free rotation is the characteristic pattern. The jolt accentuation test (worsening headache with rapid horizontal head turning) may be added in alert patients.
det.interpretation: Neck stiffness supports meningitis or subarachnoid haemorrhage but has limited sensitivity; it may be absent early, in deep coma, in infants and in older or immunocompromised patients. Resistance in all directions suggests cervical spondylosis, parkinsonism or neck pain. Tonsillar herniation can also cause neck stiffness, so fundoscopy and imaging may be needed before lumbar puncture when indicated.
pearls: Flexion-only stiffness = meningeal; all directions = mechanical or rigidity.
Absence does not exclude meningitis in coma or the elderly.
det.thd: คอแข็งเกิดจากเยื่อหุ้มสมองระคายเคืองจากการอักเสบหรือเลือด ทำให้กล้ามเนื้อคอหดเกร็งเมื่อก้มคอ แต่หันซ้ายขวาได้ปกติ ตรวจโดยยกศีรษะผู้ป่วยให้คางชิดอกแล้วลองหมุนคอ ถ้าแข็งทุกทิศทางนึกถึงโรคกระดูกคอหรือ rigidity มากกว่า ความไวไม่สูงโดยเฉพาะในผู้สูงอายุหรือผู้ป่วยหมดสติ

name: Fatigable Ptosis
formal: Ptosis that worsens with sustained upgaze and improves with rest or cooling; characteristic of neuromuscular junction transmission failure.
simple: The eyelid droops more and more when the person looks up for a while, and gets better after rest or an ice pack — typical of myasthenia gravis.
th: หนังตาตกที่มากขึ้นเมื่อมองขึ้นนาน ๆ ดีขึ้นเมื่อพักหรือประคบเย็น — นึกถึง myasthenia gravis
exam: Ask the patient to look up at your finger without blinking for 60 seconds; observe the lid margin and note new diplopia. Compare after an ice pack for 2 minutes.
pos: Progressive lid descent with sustained upgaze, improvement with ice/rest; pupils normal = neuromuscular junction disease (MG). Look for Cogan lid twitch and curtain sign.
aN: fatigable ptosis | ptosis fatigable | sustained upgaze test | simpson test | droopy eyelid

det.mechanism: In myasthenia gravis, antibody-mediated loss of acetylcholine receptors shrinks the safety factor of neuromuscular transmission. During sustained firing, the quantity of acetylcholine released per impulse normally runs down; in healthy muscle this is harmless, but in MG more and more endplate potentials fall below threshold, so fibres drop out and the levator palpebrae weakens as it works. The levator is active throughout waking hours, which helps explain why ptosis is so often the first sign and is typically worse in the evening. Lifting one lid reduces the central drive that both levators share (Hering's law), so the opposite lid may sag, and cooling slows acetylcholinesterase, which is why ice temporarily improves the lid.
det.technique: Measure the margin–reflex distance (lid edge to corneal light reflex) at rest, then ask the patient to hold gaze on a target above eye level for 60 seconds or longer without lifting the brows, and measure again, asking about diplopia as it develops. Look for Cogan lid twitch by having the patient look down for 10–15 seconds and then refixate straight ahead; a brief upward overshoot of the lid followed by drift down is positive. Lift the more ptotic lid manually to see whether the other lid falls (enhanced ptosis or curtain sign), and assess orbicularis oculi strength, since weak eye closure with a 'peek' sign strongly supports MG. An ice pack or a period of rest with eyes closed can then show reversibility. Recording the 'ptosis time' — the seconds of sustained upgaze before the lid falls — turns fatigable ptosis into a number that can be compared between visits or after treatment.
det.interpretation: Ptosis that worsens with sustained use and improves with rest or cold, with normal pupils and variable, non-anatomical ophthalmoparesis, strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction disorder, chiefly autoimmune MG including the form triggered by immune checkpoint inhibitors. Similar fatigability may occur in Lambert–Eaton syndrome (ptosis usually milder), botulism (with dilated, poorly reactive pupils and descending paralysis) and congenital myasthenic syndromes. Third nerve palsy, Horner syndrome, aponeurotic (age-related) ptosis, chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia and oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy are not genuinely fatigable, although brow strain can make a mechanical ptosis seem to tire. Fixed ptosis without ophthalmoparesis is also seen in myopathies such as myotonic dystrophy, nemaline, myofibrillar and central core myopathy, and MuSK-positive MG tends to show bulbar and neck weakness more than eye signs. A negative fatigue test does not exclude ocular MG, so serology (AChR, MuSK) and single-fibre EMG remain important.
pearls: Pupils are spared in MG; pupil involvement points to third nerve palsy or botulism.
Lift the more ptotic lid: if the other lid drops (curtain sign), think NMJ disease.
Weak eye closure plus fatigable ptosis is a strong MG combination; CPEO is slow, symmetric and non-fatigable.
Measure the lid in millimetres before and after — impressions alone are unreliable.
Note the ptosis time in seconds: a simple, repeatable measure of fatigable ptosis for follow-up.
det.thd: หนังตาตกแบบล้าได้ (fatigable ptosis) เกิดเพราะใน myasthenia gravis ตัวรับ acetylcholine ที่ NMJ ลดลง เมื่อกล้ามเนื้อยกหนังตาทำงานต่อเนื่องการส่งสัญญาณจึงล้มเหลวมากขึ้นเรื่อย ๆ ตรวจโดยวัดระยะขอบหนังตาก่อน แล้วให้มองขึ้นค้าง 60 วินาทีแล้ววัดซ้ำ ร่วมกับดู Cogan lid twitch, curtain sign และแรงหลับตา (orbicularis oculi) รูม่านตาต้องปกติ ถ้ารูม่านตาผิดปกตินึกถึง third nerve palsy หรือ botulism ส่วน Horner, หนังตาตกจากอายุ และ CPEO ไม่ล้าตามการใช้งาน ผลลบไม่ตัด ocular MG ควรตรวจแอนติบอดีและ EMG ประกอบ

name: Horner Syndrome
formal: Ipsilateral mild ptosis, miosis with dilation lag and variable facial anhidrosis from interruption of the oculosympathetic pathway (hypothalamus → brainstem → cord → sympathetic chain → carotid plexus).
simple: A small pupil, slightly droopy eyelid and sometimes reduced facial sweating, all on one side, due to damage to the nerve pathway that runs from the brain down the neck and back up to the eye.
th: หนังตาตกเล็กน้อย รูม่านตาเล็ก เหงื่อออกน้อยข้างเดียวกัน — เส้นทางประสาท sympathetic ไปตาเสียหาย
exam: Compare pupils in bright and dim light (anisocoria greater in the dark), look for dilation lag, upper and lower lid ptosis, and check facial sweating.
pos: Central (stroke/demyelination, with other brainstem signs), preganglionic (lung apex, neck trauma) or postganglionic (carotid dissection, cluster headache). Painful acute Horner = carotid dissection until proven otherwise.
aN: horner | horner syndrome | oculosympathetic palsy | bernard horner

det.mechanism: The oculosympathetic pathway is a three-neuron chain: from the hypothalamus through the lateral brainstem to the C8–T2 cord (first order), across the lung apex up to the superior cervical ganglion (second order), then travelling alongside the internal carotid artery through the cavernous sinus into the orbit (third order). Interruption anywhere weakens the pupil dilator and Müller's muscle, giving miosis and mild ptosis, with anhidrosis depending on the level.
det.technique: Examine pupils in bright and then dim light; anisocoria that increases in darkness with slow re-dilation of the small pupil (dilation lag) supports Horner. Look for slight upper lid ptosis and lower lid elevation (upside-down ptosis). Pharmacological testing with apraclonidine (reversal of anisocoria) or cocaine confirms the diagnosis; hydroxyamphetamine helps localise third-order lesions.
det.interpretation: Associated features localise the lesion: brainstem signs (lateral medullary syndrome), myelopathy, arm pain or hand wasting (Pancoast tumour, lower trunk plexopathy), or neck pain and headache (carotid dissection). Anhidrosis of the whole half body or face suggests central or preganglionic lesions; postganglionic lesions spare most facial sweating. Congenital Horner causes iris heterochromia. Physiological anisocoria lacks ptosis and dilation lag.
pearls: Acute painful Horner = carotid dissection until imaging says otherwise.
Anisocoria worse in the dark points to the small pupil as abnormal.
Look for a Pancoast tumour in smokers with shoulder pain and Horner.
det.thd: Horner syndrome เกิดจากเส้นทางประสาท sympathetic ไปตา 3 ช่วง (สมอง-ไขสันหลัง, ยอดปอด-คอ, ตามหลอดเลือด carotid) ถูกขัดขวาง ทำให้รูม่านตาเล็ก หนังตาตกเล็กน้อย และอาจเหงื่อออกน้อย ตรวจในที่มืดจะเห็นรูม่านตาต่างกันมากขึ้นและขยายช้า อาการร่วมช่วยบอกตำแหน่ง ถ้าเกิดฉับพลันร่วมกับปวดคอ/ปวดหัวต้องคิดถึง carotid dissection ก่อน

name: Relative Afferent Pupillary Defect (RAPD)
formal: Paradoxical dilation of both pupils when a light is swung from the normal to the affected eye, indicating asymmetric afferent (optic nerve or extensive retinal) dysfunction.
simple: When a torch swings from one eye to the other, both pupils widen when the light reaches the damaged eye — showing that eye's optic nerve passes less light signal.
th: ส่องไฟสลับตา เมื่อไฟมาที่ตาข้างผิดปกติรูม่านตาทั้งสองขยาย — บ่งชี้เส้นประสาทตาข้างนั้นเสีย
exam: In a dim room, swing a bright light briskly between the eyes, pausing 2–3 seconds on each.
pos: Dilation on illumination of one eye = afferent defect in that eye (optic neuritis, ischaemic optic neuropathy, compression). Cataract does not cause RAPD.
aN: rapd | relative afferent pupillary defect | marcus gunn pupil | swinging flashlight test | afferent pupillary defect

det.mechanism: Pupillomotor axons travel with the visual fibres through the optic nerve, chiasm and tract, then peel off before the lateral geniculate body to reach both pretectal nuclei, each of which feeds both Edinger–Westphal nuclei. Because the output is shared, a light in either eye normally tightens both pupils to the same extent, and the pupils stay equal in size even when one afferent limb is damaged. When one eye delivers a weaker signal, the summed drive falls whenever that eye is the one illuminated, so on swinging the beam across, both pupils relax outward instead of constricting further. The sign therefore measures an imbalance of afferent input, not any fault of the iris or the third nerve.
det.technique: Darken the room, ask the patient to look at a distant target to avoid near-reflex miosis, and use a bright, evenly focused light. Move the beam briskly across the nasal bridge, resting about 2–3 seconds on each eye, and judge the initial movement of the pupil being lit over several cycles, since a single swing is easily misread. If one pupil cannot react (fixed third nerve palsy, pharmacological mydriasis, trauma, synechiae), watch only the working pupil throughout — the reverse or consensual method: if it dilates as the beam moves onto the fellow eye, the afferent defect is in the fellow eye, and if it dilates as the beam returns to itself, the defect is on its own side. To grade, place neutral density filters of rising strength (usually 0.3 to about 1.8 log units) over the better eye until the swing looks balanced, and record the log-unit value; a cruder bedside scale of 1+ to 4+ is also used.
det.interpretation: An RAPD means asymmetric afferent conduction anterior to the geniculate: unilateral or unequal optic neuropathy (demyelinating, ischaemic, compressive, inflammatory, traumatic, glaucomatous), or retinal disease extensive enough to be obvious on fundoscopy, such as a large detachment or central retinal artery occlusion. A unilateral optic tract lesion gives a modest RAPD in the contralateral eye — the eye that has lost its temporal hemifield, which normally supplies more pupillomotor drive — together with a homonymous hemianopia, and lesions in the pretectum, or in the fibre bundle running to the superior colliculus, can produce a contralateral RAPD with no visual loss at all. Lesions of the lateral geniculate, optic radiations or occipital cortex do not cause an RAPD, nor do cataract, corneal scarring, refractive error, mild macular disease or functional visual loss; a very dense cataract may even give a small RAPD in the opposite eye that vanishes after surgery. Amblyopia and vitreous haemorrhage only occasionally produce a mild defect, anisocoria above about 2 mm can create a small spurious RAPD in the smaller pupil, and equal bilateral optic neuropathy may show none.
pearls: Media opacity, refractive error and functional loss never explain an RAPD; one found behind a cataract means look at the nerve or retina.
A fixed pupil does not stop the test: watch the reactive pupil (reverse RAPD).
Optic tract lesion: mild RAPD in the eye contralateral to the lesion plus a homonymous field defect; pretectal lesions may give one with normal vision.
RAPD size follows field loss more than acuity, and symmetric bilateral disease can hide it.
det.thd: RAPD เกิดเพราะเส้นประสาทตาหรือจอตาข้างหนึ่งส่งสัญญาณแสงไปยัง pretectal nucleus ได้น้อยกว่า เมื่อส่องไฟสลับจากตาดีไปตาที่เสีย รูม่านตาทั้งสองข้างจึงขยายแทนที่จะหด ตรวจในห้องมืดให้มองไกล ส่องสลับข้างละ 2–3 วินาทีหลายรอบ ถ้ารูม่านตาข้างหนึ่งขยับไม่ได้ให้ดูรูม่านตาข้างที่ดีแทน (reverse RAPD) และวัดความรุนแรงได้ด้วย neutral density filter วางหน้าตาดี ผลบวกบ่งชี้ optic neuropathy, จอตาเสียกว้าง หรือรอยโรค optic tract (RAPD ที่ตาด้านตรงข้ามรอยโรค) ส่วนต้อกระจก สายตาผิดปกติ รอยโรคหลัง LGN และ functional visual loss ไม่ทำให้เกิด RAPD

name: Dysdiadochokinesia
formal: Impaired performance of rapid alternating movements (e.g. pronation–supination), with irregular rhythm and amplitude; a sign of ipsilateral cerebellar hemisphere dysfunction.
simple: Difficulty quickly flipping the hand back and forth — the movements become clumsy and uneven, pointing to a problem in the cerebellum on the same side.
th: พลิกมือคว่ำหงายเร็ว ๆ ไม่สม่ำเสมอ — บ่งชี้สมองน้อยข้างเดียวกันผิดปกติ
exam: Ask the patient to tap the palm and back of one hand alternately on the other palm or thigh as fast as possible; compare sides.
pos: Irregular rhythm/force = ipsilateral cerebellar lesion. Slow but rhythmic with decrement suggests parkinsonism; slow due to weakness suggests UMN.
aN: dysdiadochokinesis | rapid alternating movements | adiadochokinesia

det.mechanism: Rapid alternating movements require precise timing of agonist cessation and antagonist onset. The cerebellum predicts and coordinates these switches; when it is damaged, timing and force become variable, so movements lose rhythm and amplitude consistency. Cerebellar hemispheres control the ipsilateral limbs.
det.technique: Ask the patient to pat one hand on the other palm or thigh, alternating palm and back, as fast and regularly as possible, and listen as well as look; repeat with the other hand. In the legs, ask for rapid foot tapping. Compare sides and note slowing versus irregularity, since weakness or rigidity slow movements without causing dysrhythmia.
det.interpretation: Irregular rhythm, force and range indicate ipsilateral cerebellar or cerebellar pathway dysfunction, as in MS, stroke, alcohol-related or degenerative ataxia. Progressive slowing and decreasing amplitude (decrement) suggest parkinsonism. Pure slowness with otherwise smooth rhythm is seen with UMN weakness. The non-dominant hand is normally slightly slower.
pearls: Listen to the rhythm — the irregular sound is often more obvious than the look.
Decrement = parkinsonism; dysrhythmia = cerebellum.
det.thd: Dysdiadochokinesia คือทำการเคลื่อนไหวสลับเร็ว ๆ ได้ไม่สม่ำเสมอ เพราะสมองน้อยควบคุมจังหวะการเปลี่ยนกล้ามเนื้อหดและคลายไม่ได้ ตรวจโดยให้ตบมือคว่ำหงายบนฝ่ามืออีกข้างเร็ว ๆ แล้วฟังจังหวะเทียบสองข้าง ถ้าจังหวะและแรงไม่สม่ำเสมอบ่งชี้สมองน้อยข้างเดียวกัน ถ้าช้าลงและแคบลงเรื่อย ๆ นึกถึง parkinsonism

name: Intention Tremor
formal: Tremor that increases in amplitude as the limb approaches a target during finger–nose or heel–shin testing, reflecting cerebellar or cerebellar outflow dysfunction.
simple: The hand shakes more and more as it gets close to a target, like touching the nose — a cerebellum problem.
th: มือสั่นมากขึ้นเมื่อเข้าใกล้เป้าหมาย — บ่งชี้สมองน้อยหรือทางออกของสมองน้อยผิดปกติ
exam: Finger–nose–finger test with a moving target; heel–knee–shin in the legs.
pos: Oscillation increasing near the target with dysmetria = ipsilateral cerebellar hemisphere/superior cerebellar peduncle (MS, stroke, Wilson, alcohol).
aN: intention tremor | cerebellar tremor | terminal tremor | finger nose ataxia | past pointing

det.mechanism: As a limb approaches a target, the cerebellum normally applies fine predictive corrections. Lesions of the cerebellar hemispheres, dentate nucleus or superior cerebellar peduncle cause over- and under-correction, producing a coarse oscillation perpendicular to the line of movement that grows near the target, together with dysmetria.
det.technique: Have the patient move a fingertip from their own nose to your finger, moving your finger to new positions at full arm's reach, and repeat with eyes open. Observe amplitude through the movement and at the endpoint. Test the heel–knee–shin manoeuvre in the legs. Make the patient reach fully, as short movements may hide the tremor.
det.interpretation: Increasing tremor near the target indicates ipsilateral cerebellar or cerebellar outflow pathway disease, often from MS, stroke, tumour, alcohol or drug toxicity (e.g. lithium, phenytoin). Essential tremor can develop an intentional component in advanced cases. Holmes tremor combines rest, postural and intention components after midbrain/thalamic lesions. Functional tremor typically varies with distraction and entrains.
pearls: Tremor grows as the target nears; check both directions of finger–nose.
Check for lithium or antiepileptic toxicity in new cerebellar signs.
det.thd: Intention tremor คือมือสั่นมากขึ้นเมื่อเข้าใกล้เป้าหมาย เกิดเพราะสมองน้อยหรือทางออกของสมองน้อยแก้ไขทิศทางการเคลื่อนไหวไม่แม่นยำ ตรวจด้วย finger–nose–finger โดยให้เอื้อมสุดแขนและขยับเป้าหมาย และ heel–knee–shin ที่ขา พบใน MS, stroke, สุรา หรือพิษยา เช่น lithium, phenytoin

name: Fasciculations
formal: Visible spontaneous twitches of a motor unit beneath the skin; with weakness and wasting they indicate lower motor neuron (anterior horn) disease.
simple: Small flickering twitches under the skin, like worms moving; when combined with weakness and thin muscles they point to motor nerve cell disease.
th: กล้ามเนื้อเต้นพลิ้วใต้ผิวหนัง — ถ้ามีร่วมกับอ่อนแรง/ลีบ บ่งชี้ LMN หรือเซลล์ประสาทสั่งการเสื่อม
exam: Observe relaxed, exposed muscles in good light for at least 1–2 minutes per region; inspect the tongue resting in the mouth (not protruded).
pos: Widespread fasciculations with wasting = anterior horn cell disease (ALS, SMA, Kennedy). Isolated without weakness is often benign.
aN: fasciculation | muscle twitching | tongue fasciculation | fasciculations

det.mechanism: A fasciculation results from spontaneous firing of one motor unit, originating in the distal axon, the nerve terminal or, less often, the cell body. In motor neuron disease, degenerating and reinnervating motor axons become hyperexcitable and fire ectopically. Because entire motor units contract, the twitch is visible through the skin but too small to move a joint.
det.technique: Expose large muscle groups (shoulder girdle, thighs, calves, abdomen) and observe each for at least a minute in good tangential light with the muscle relaxed. Inspect the tongue resting on the floor of the mouth, not protruded, because protrusion produces normal tremulous movements. Gentle tapping can provoke them; EMG and ultrasound detect deeper ones.
det.interpretation: Fasciculations with wasting, weakness and especially brisk reflexes suggest ALS; with wasting and absent reflexes, consider SMA, Kennedy disease or chronic radiculopathy. Benign fasciculations without weakness, wasting or EMG abnormality are common in healthy people, often in calves or eyelids, and linked to caffeine, stress and exercise. Cramp-fasciculation syndrome, thyrotoxicosis, hypomagnesaemia and anticholinesterase drugs are other causes.
pearls: Fasciculations alone without weakness or wasting are usually benign.
Examine the tongue at rest inside the mouth.
Tongue fasciculation is valuable for bulbar ALS; also check facial and perioral twitching in Kennedy disease.
det.thd: Fasciculation คือการเต้นของกล้ามเนื้อทั้ง motor unit ที่เกิดเองจากใยประสาทสั่งการที่ไวผิดปกติ มองเห็นเป็นพลิ้วใต้ผิวหนัง ให้สังเกตกล้ามเนื้อที่ผ่อนคลายนาน 1–2 นาทีและดูลิ้นขณะวางในปาก (ไม่แลบ) ถ้ามีร่วมกับลีบอ่อนแรงนึกถึง ALS หรือ SMA แต่ถ้าไม่มีอ่อนแรงมักเป็นแบบ benign เช่น จากกาแฟ ความเครียด หรือหลังออกกำลังกาย

name: Scapular Winging
formal: Protrusion of the medial border or inferior angle of the scapula away from the chest wall, from weakness of a scapular stabiliser (serratus anterior, trapezius, rhomboids); in FSHD it is asymmetric and the shoulder blade also rides upward and outward on arm elevation.
simple: The shoulder blade sticks out like a wing from the back when the patient pushes against a wall or lifts the arms, because the muscles that hold it flat are weak.
th: สะบักยื่นออกจากผนังทรวงอกคล้ายปีก เกิดจากกล้ามเนื้อยึดสะบักอ่อนแรง เช่น serratus anterior หรือ trapezius ใน FSHD มักเป็นไม่เท่ากันสองข้างและสะบักเลื่อนขึ้นเมื่อยกแขน
exam: Inspect the back with the patient standing, arms hanging, then ask for forward arm elevation to 90 degrees and a wall push-up. Medial winging (serratus anterior, long thoracic nerve) is worst on forward push; lateral winging (trapezius, spinal accessory nerve) is worse on abduction. In FSHD the scapula may also glide upward when the arm is raised, and the winging is unilateral or asymmetric.
pos: Medial winging with a long thoracic nerve lesion or brachial neuritis; lateral winging with spinal accessory injury or C3-C4 root disease; global winging with weakness of several scapular muscles in FSHD, some limb girdle dystrophies, polyneuropathy or generalised myasthenia. Asymmetric winging with facial weakness and sparing of the deltoid is typical of FSHD.
aN: winged scapula | scapula alata | medial scapular winging | lateral scapular winging | scapular fixator weakness

det.mechanism: The scapula is held against the rib cage by a sling of muscles: serratus anterior pulls the medial border forward, trapezius and rhomboids pull it medially and upward, and levator scapulae and latissimus dorsi steady its angle. When one of these fails the unopposed pull of the others lifts a part of the blade off the chest wall. Serratus anterior loss produces medial winging, trapezius loss gives lateral displacement with a drooping shoulder, and in FSHD the weakness is muscular, affects several stabilisers and is asymmetric, so the scapula also rides up on arm elevation.
det.technique: Inspect the back with the shoulders relaxed, then ask for forward flexion to 90 degrees, a wall push-up and slow lowering of the arms from overhead. Resisted pushing forward brings out medial winging; resisted abduction and shoulder shrug bring out lateral winging. Photograph or video the back, as the shape is easy to under-call when the patient is dressed. Common errors are mistaking a thoracic scoliosis or a rotator cuff problem for winging, and failing to check both sides.
det.interpretation: Medial winging points to a long thoracic nerve lesion, Parsonage-Turner syndrome (brachial neuritis), and some muscular dystrophies; lateral winging points to the spinal accessory nerve or trapezius, or a C3-C4 root lesion. Asymmetric winging with facial weakness, preserved deltoid, abdominal weakness and foot drop is the FSHD picture, whereas symmetric winging with proximal weakness and high CK points to limb girdle dystrophy, such as calpainopathy, or Pompe disease. Electrodiagnosis and muscle MRI distinguish neurogenic from myopathic causes.
pearls: Medial winging is worse on pushing forward; lateral winging is worse on abduction.
Asymmetric winging plus facial weakness and sparing of the deltoid = FSHD until proven otherwise.
Look for the second sign: the scapula that rises with arm elevation in FSHD.
det.thd: Scapular winging คือสะบักยื่นออกจากทรวงอกเพราะกล้ามเนื้อยึดสะบักอ่อนแรง ให้ผู้ป่วยยกแขนไปข้างหน้าหรือดันกำแพงแล้วดูด้านหลัง ถ้ายื่นด้านใน (medial) นึกถึง long thoracic nerve หรือ brachial neuritis ถ้ายื่นด้านข้าง (lateral) นึกถึง spinal accessory nerve ส่วน FSHD มักเป็นสองข้างไม่เท่ากันร่วมกับกล้ามเนื้อใบหน้าอ่อนแรงและ deltoid ยังดี

name: Transverse Smile
formal: A smile that spreads horizontally with little upward lift of the mouth corners because the zygomaticus muscles and orbicularis oris are weak while risorius is relatively preserved; characteristic of facial involvement in FSHD.
simple: The smile stretches sideways like a flat line instead of curving up, because the muscles that raise the corners of the mouth are weak.
th: ยิ้มแล้วมุมปากไม่ยกขึ้น ปากยืดออกด้านข้างเป็นเส้นตรง เกิดจากกล้ามเนื้อ zygomaticus และ orbicularis oris อ่อนแรง พบใน FSHD
exam: Ask the patient to smile broadly, whistle, purse the lips, puff the cheeks and close the eyes tightly against resistance. Note whether the mouth corners rise, whether eyelashes are buried and whether the lips are able to hold air. Check the eye closure during sleep or by asking the family.
pos: A horizontal smile with difficulty whistling, drinking through a straw or burying the eyelashes suggests facial weakness of FSHD; a similar flat smile occurs in myasthenia (myasthenic snarl) and myotonic dystrophy. The extraocular muscles and eyelid are spared in FSHD, and ptosis suggests another diagnosis.
aN: horizontal smile | snarling smile | fshd smile | flat smile | risorius smile

det.mechanism: A normal smile lifts the corners of the mouth upward and outward by zygomaticus major and minor and levator labii, with orbicularis oris holding the lips together. In FSHD these muscles, and orbicularis oculi, are among the first to weaken, while risorius and platysma retain strength. Their unopposed pull draws the mouth straight sideways, giving a horizontal or snarl-like smile.
det.technique: Ask the patient to smile naturally, then widely, and to say 'ee' and 'oo', whistle, puff the cheeks and suck through a straw. Test eye closure with the eyelids held open against resistance, and ask relatives whether the eyes stay slightly open in sleep. Compare with old photographs, which often show the change before the patient has noticed.
det.interpretation: A transverse smile with weak whistling and lip pursing and incomplete eye closure is characteristic of FSHD, and is often present before limb weakness. It is not specific: the myasthenic snarl, myotonic dystrophy with its long thin face, and some congenital myopathies produce a flattened smile. Ptosis, extraocular muscle weakness or marked bulbar involvement are red flags against FSHD.
pearls: Ask about whistling and drinking through a straw.
Spared ptosis and eye movements fit FSHD.
Check old photographs and eye closure in sleep.
det.thd: Transverse smile คือการยิ้มที่มุมปากไม่ยกขึ้นแต่ยืดออกด้านข้าง เพราะกล้ามเนื้อ zygomaticus และ orbicularis oris อ่อนแรง พบใน FSHD ร่วมกับผิวปากไม่ได้และหลับตาไม่สนิท ควรถามผู้ป่วยและเทียบกับรูปเก่า และนึกถึงโรคอื่น เช่น myasthenia gravis หรือ myotonic dystrophy ถ้ามีหนังตาตกหรือกล้ามเนื้อตาอ่อนแรง

name: Poly-Hill Sign
formal: Altered shoulder contour in FSHD: trapezius wasting with upward displacement of the scapula, a prominent acromioclavicular joint, and wasting of the proximal deltoid and biceps with a relatively spared distal deltoid, producing a sloping, bulging outline.
simple: A characteristic shoulder shape in FSHD: the neck-to-shoulder line slopes, the collarbone joint sticks out and the upper arm looks thin while the lower part of the deltoid stays full.
th: รูปร่างไหล่เฉพาะของ FSHD ได้แก่ trapezius ลีบ สะบักยกสูง ข้อ acromioclavicular นูน และต้นแขนส่วนบนลีบ แต่ส่วนปลายของ deltoid ยังคงขนาดอยู่
exam: Look at the patient from the front and behind with the arms relaxed. Compare the slope from neck to acromion, the height of the acromioclavicular joint, and the bulk of the upper deltoid and biceps with the lower deltoid. Add resisted shoulder abduction and arm elevation to see how the scapula rides.
pos: The combination of a sloping trapezius contour, a prominent acromioclavicular joint and wasted upper arm with preserved distal deltoid is a strong visual clue to FSHD and is usually asymmetric. Spared deltoid strength despite scapular winging also separates FSHD from many limb girdle dystrophies.
aN: polyhill sign | poly hill sign | polyhill | fshd shoulder contour | trapezius squaring

det.mechanism: In FSHD the trapezius is often wasted early, so the scapula is pulled upward and outward by unopposed levator scapulae, and the acromioclavicular joint stands out. The proximal portion of the deltoid and the biceps and triceps are involved earlier than the distal deltoid and the forearm, which gives the upper arm a thin, tapered contour above a fuller lower deltoid. The result is a characteristic sloping and uneven shoulder silhouette.
det.technique: Examine from the front, the side and behind, with the arms relaxed and then abducted. Compare the neck-shoulder slope, the prominence of the acromioclavicular joint, and the bulk of upper compared with lower deltoid on each side; the changes are usually asymmetric. Pair this inspection with scapular winging, shoulder abduction strength and the Popeye arm contour.
det.interpretation: The sign points to FSHD and may be seen before the patient complains of weakness. It has not been validated by sensitivity studies, so use it as a pattern clue to prompt genetic testing. Look-alikes include chronic accessory nerve injury and long-standing brachial neuritis, which affect a single nerve territory and not the face.
pearls: Sloping trapezius + prominent AC joint + thin upper arm with spared lower deltoid.
Asymmetry is the rule in FSHD.
det.thd: Poly-Hill sign คือลักษณะรูปร่างไหล่ของ FSHD ได้แก่ trapezius ลีบ สะบักยกสูง ข้อ acromioclavicular นูน ต้นแขนส่วนบนและ biceps ลีบ แต่ deltoid ส่วนปลายยังคงอยู่ มักไม่เท่ากันสองข้าง ใช้เป็นเบาะแสให้ส่งตรวจพันธุกรรม FSHD

name: Bow-Tie Atrophy
formal: Horizontal band-shaped pallor of the optic disc across its nasal and temporal sectors, with preserved superior and inferior rims, due to loss of nasal retinal (crossing) fibres from a chiasmal or optic tract lesion.
simple: When the optic nerve head is examined, the pale area forms a horizontal bow-tie across the disc after the crossing nerve fibres have been destroyed, for example by a tumour pressing on the optic chiasm.
th: จานประสาทตาซีดเป็นแถบแนวนอนด้านนาสิกและขมับคล้ายโบว์ไท ขอบบนและล่างยังดี จากการสูญเสียเส้นใยที่ไขว้ที่ chiasm หรือ optic tract
exam: Dilated fundus examination of both eyes, comparing disc colour in all four sectors, with a good light and a direct ophthalmoscope or fundus photograph. Confirm with optical coherence tomography (peripapillary fibre layer thickness) and map the visual fields.
pos: In chiasmal lesions (pituitary tumour, craniopharyngioma, meningioma) both eyes may show band pallor with bitemporal field defects. A lesion of the optic tract produces band atrophy and an afferent pupillary defect (RAPD) on the contralateral side, with an incongruous homonymous hemianopia. Preserved superior and inferior disc sectors distinguish it from diffuse pallor of optic neuritis and compressive optic neuropathy.
aN: band atrophy | band shaped optic atrophy | bow tie pallor | horizontal band optic atrophy | optic disc bow tie pallor

det.mechanism: Retinal ganglion cell axons from the nasal retina cross at the chiasm and are the first to be lost with chiasmal compression, while fibres from the temporal retina remain. Fibres from the nasal retina and from the nasal macular region project to the nasal and temporal (papillomacular) sectors of the disc, so these sectors turn pale, whereas the superior and inferior rims carry mostly uncrossed temporal retinal fibres and stay pink. In optic tract damage the contralateral eye loses its crossed nasal fibres and shows a band pattern, while the ipsilateral eye loses temporal fibres and often looks less distinctive.
det.technique: Dilate the pupils and examine each disc systematically in four quadrants, comparing colour and rim sharpness. Fundus photographs help follow change over time. Use optical coherence tomography, where thinning of the peripapillary fibre layer and the macular ganglion cell complex shows the same band pattern, and correlate with automated perimetry, looking for bitemporal or incongruous homonymous field defects.
det.interpretation: Band atrophy indicates damage posterior to the retinal ganglion cell body and the optic nerve head, most often from chiasmal compression (pituitary adenoma, craniopharyngioma, meningioma) or a retrochiasmal lesion. Combined with a bitemporal hemianopia it is a strong indication for MRI of the sella and chiasm. Pallor appears only weeks to months after the injury, so a normal disc does not exclude a recent compressive lesion.
pearls: Band pallor with bitemporal field loss = chiasmal compression until MRI says otherwise.
Disc pallor lags weeks to months behind the lesion.
A unilateral band in the contralateral eye with a RAPD suggests an optic tract lesion.
det.thd: Bow-tie atrophy คือจานประสาทตาซีดเป็นแถบแนวนอนคล้ายโบว์ไท เกิดจากการสูญเสียเส้นใยที่ไขว้ที่ chiasm จากเนื้องอก เช่น pituitary tumour หรือ craniopharyngioma มักพบพร้อมลานสายตาเสียแบบ bitemporal ควรตรวจ MRI sella และ chiasm และต้องจำว่าจานประสาทตาจะซีดช้ากว่ารอยโรคหลายสัปดาห์

name: Helicopter Sign
formal: A fast, regular thumping or whirring sound heard over the thigh or calf with a stethoscope, or from EMG audio, of the 13 to 18 Hz leg muscle discharge in primary orthostatic tremor.
simple: Listening with a stethoscope on the thigh of a patient who feels shaky when standing, you hear a fast rhythmic chopping noise like a distant helicopter, which shows the fine leg tremor.
th: ฟังเสียงที่ต้นขาหรือน่องด้วย stethoscope ขณะผู้ป่วยยืน จะได้ยินเสียงรัวเร็วสม่ำเสมอคล้ายเฮลิคอปเตอร์ เป็นเสียงของ orthostatic tremor ที่ความถี่ประมาณ 13–18 Hz
exam: Ask the patient to stand without support for at least a minute (the tremor builds up) and place the diaphragm of a stethoscope on the quadriceps or gastrocnemius; listen again after the patient sits, walks or leans on a support. Confirm and quantify with surface EMG of both legs.
pos: A fast, regular chopping sound while standing that fades on sitting or when the weight is borne by a support is characteristic of orthostatic tremor. A slower, visible leg tremor under 13 Hz suggests pseudo-orthostatic tremor, and irregular brief twitches suggest orthostatic myoclonus, so the sound does not replace EMG. The curator's notes pair the sign with the orthostatic myoclonus differential; the standard teaching attaches it to orthostatic tremor.
aN: helicopter sound | stethoscope sign of orthostatic tremor | thigh auscultation sign | auscultation of orthostatic tremor

det.mechanism: Primary orthostatic tremor consists of a very fast, regular 13 to 18 Hz burst in the leg and trunk muscles during stance, driven by a central oscillator, which is too fast to produce visible shaking. The synchronous repeated contractions create a low-pitched vibration that can be heard through a stethoscope as a regular whirring noise. The same signal played from EMG through a loudspeaker sounds like a helicopter.
det.technique: Have the patient stand unsupported for a minute or more, since the tremor builds up with time, then place the stethoscope diaphragm on the thigh (quadriceps) or calf. Listen again after sitting, leaning on a rail or walking. Always follow with EMG, which gives the frequency, compares left and right legs, and checks for coherence between muscles.
det.interpretation: A steady helicopter-like sound confirms a very fast rhythmic activity and supports primary orthostatic tremor, which is reported to improve on walking. It cannot tell the frequency, so slow orthostatic tremor of 4 to 10 Hz (pseudo-orthostatic tremor) and irregular myoclonic bursts must be separated with EMG. A negative sign does not exclude orthostatic tremor if the patient does not stand long enough. The curator's myoclonus notes pair the term with orthostatic myoclonus; the standard textbook usage is for orthostatic tremor.
pearls: Listen after at least a minute of unsupported standing.
Sound heard + EMG 13 to 18 Hz = orthostatic tremor.
Irregular brief bursts on EMG that worsen with walking = orthostatic myoclonus instead.
det.thd: Helicopter sign คือเสียงรัวเร็วสม่ำเสมอคล้ายเฮลิคอปเตอร์ที่ฟังได้เหนือต้นขาหรือน่องด้วย stethoscope ขณะผู้ป่วยยืนนิ่ง เป็นลักษณะของ orthostatic tremor ที่ความถี่ 13–18 Hz ซึ่งเร็วเกินกว่าจะมองเห็น ควรให้ยืนนานพอ แล้วยืนยันด้วย EMG เพราะเสียงไม่บอกความถี่และไม่แยกจาก pseudo-orthostatic tremor หรือ orthostatic myoclonus

name: Cornea Verticillata (Corneal Whorls)
formal: Fine cream-to-golden or grey deposits in the corneal epithelium arranged in a whorl or vortex pattern radiating from a point below the pupil; classically seen in Fabry disease, and also from drugs such as amiodarone, chloroquine and hydroxychloroquine.
simple: Slit-lamp view of tiny swirling lines on the front of the cornea, like the pattern of a fingerprint. It is an early clue to Fabry disease but can also be caused by some medicines.
th: ตะกอนละเอียดรูปก้นหอยที่เยื่อบุผิวกระจกตา เห็นด้วย slit lamp เป็นเบาะแสสำคัญของโรค Fabry และพบจากยา เช่น amiodarone และ chloroquine ได้ ไม่ทำให้การมองเห็นเสีย
exam: Ask for slit-lamp examination by an ophthalmologist, ideally before pupil dilation. Look at the corneal epithelium with a narrow beam and indirect illumination for a whorl radiating from below the pupil. Take a medication history (amiodarone, hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine, tamoxifen).
pos: Whorl-like opacities in a young patient with acral burning pain, hypohidrosis or proteinuria support Fabry disease, and are present in hemizygous men and in many heterozygous women. Drug-induced whorls look the same, so do not diagnose Fabry on this sign alone.
aN: corneal whorls | cornea verticillata | vortex keratopathy | whorl like keratopathy | fabry corneal dystrophy

det.mechanism: In Fabry disease globotriaosylceramide builds up inside the basal epithelial cells of the cornea because of alpha-galactosidase A deficiency. The deposits spread along the migration paths of epithelial cells from the limbus, which draws a whorl that radiates outward from a point just below the pupil. Cationic amphiphilic drugs create the same picture by trapping phospholipids in the same cells.
det.technique: Request a slit-lamp exam by an ophthalmologist, preferably before dilation, using a narrow beam and indirect or retro-illumination. The deposits are tiny and cannot be seen with a hand-held ophthalmoscope in most patients. Record any amiodarone, hydroxychloroquine or chloroquine use.
det.interpretation: Whorls appear early, occur in nearly all affected men and many women with Fabry disease, and are not associated with a loss of acuity. They support, but do not prove, Fabry disease because drug-induced whorls are identical. Posterior lens opacities and tortuous conjunctival vessels may accompany them.
pearls: Always ask about amiodarone and hydroxychloroquine before attributing whorls to Fabry disease.
Whorls are a useful screening sign in women with equivocal enzyme activity.
det.thd: Cornea verticillata คือตะกอนรูปก้นหอยในเยื่อบุผิวกระจกตา เกิดจาก Gb3 สะสมในโรค Fabry หรือจากยา เช่น amiodarone และ hydroxychloroquine ต้องตรวจด้วย slit lamp โดยจักษุแพทย์ ช่วยสนับสนุนการวินิจฉัย Fabry แต่ไม่ยืนยัน และมักไม่กระทบการมองเห็น

name: Angiokeratoma
formal: Dark red to blue-black, non-blanching punctate papules a few millimetres across, typically clustered in the lower trunk (bathing-trunk area), umbilicus, buttocks and thighs; the cutaneous marker of Fabry disease when numerous and starting in childhood or adolescence.
simple: Tiny dark red spots on the skin that do not fade when pressed, clustered around the belly button, hips and thighs. When many appear in a young person with burning hands and feet, think Fabry disease.
th: ตุ่มแดงเข้มถึงม่วงดำขนาดเล็ก กดไม่จาง พบเป็นกลุ่มบริเวณสะดือ สะโพก ต้นขา เมื่อพบมากในเด็กหรือวัยรุ่นที่ปวดแสบมือเท้า ควรนึกถึงโรค Fabry
exam: Inspect the skin between the umbilicus and the knees, including the buttocks, scrotum, groin and thighs, with good light. Press with a glass slide to show that the papules do not blanch. Count and map them; check the mouth and conjunctiva for telangiectasia.
pos: Multiple punctate non-blanching papules in a bathing-trunk pattern in a child or young adult with acral pain suggest Fabry disease, although some patients, especially women, have none. Solitary or scrotal angiokeratomas in older adults are common and often unrelated to Fabry disease; other causes include fucosidosis and sialidosis.
aN: angiokeratoma corporis diffusum | fabry skin lesions | bathing trunk angiokeratomas | fordyce angiokeratoma not fabry | telangiectatic papules of fabry

det.mechanism: Angiokeratomas are dilated capillaries in the upper dermis with overlying epidermal thickening. In Fabry disease, Gb3 accumulates in dermal vascular endothelium and pericytes, causing capillary ectasia that shows as dark red papules. The lower trunk is affected first because of local temperature and pressure.
det.technique: Examine under good light the skin from navel to knees, including the groin, buttocks and thighs, and press with a glass slide to show non-blanching. Document count and location with photos for follow-up. Also look at oral mucosa for telangiectasia.
det.interpretation: Numerous clustered papules beginning in childhood or adolescence are a strong clue to Fabry disease, and usually increase with age. Their absence does not exclude the disease, especially in women. Isolated angiokeratomas of the scrotum or lower limbs in older adults are often benign; fucosidosis and other lysosomal diseases also produce angiokeratomas.
pearls: Undress the patient to the knees when considering Fabry disease.
Absence of skin lesions does not rule out Fabry disease, particularly in women.
det.thd: Angiokeratoma คือตุ่มหลอดเลือดฝอยขยายสีแดงเข้มถึงม่วงดำ กดไม่จาง พบบริเวณสะดือถึงเข่า ในโรค Fabry เกิดจาก Gb3 สะสมในหลอดเลือด ควรตรวจผิวหนังในผู้ป่วยที่ปวดแสบมือเท้าตั้งแต่เด็ก แต่ถ้าไม่พบก็ไม่ตัดโรคออก โดยเฉพาะในผู้หญิง

name: Trident Sign (Spinal Cord Sarcoidosis)
formal: Axial post-gadolinium MRI appearance of the spinal cord with enhancement of the dorsal subpial surface together with enhancement of the central canal, forming a three-pronged pattern; considered a hallmark of sarcoid myelopathy and rare in other causes of long myelitis.
simple: On an MRI slice across the spinal cord, bright contrast forms a three-pointed shape (like a trident or pitchfork) at the back and middle of the cord. It points strongly towards sarcoidosis.
ab: dorsal subpial and central canal enhancement
th: ภาพ MRI ตัดขวางไขสันหลังหลังให้สารทึบแสง เห็นการ enhance ที่ผิวด้านหลัง (dorsal subpial) ร่วมกับ central canal เป็นรูปสามง่ามคล้าย trident บ่งชี้ sarcoid myelopathy
exam: Not a bedside sign: after a longitudinally extensive T2 lesion is found, obtain thin axial post-gadolinium T1 images through the lesion and look for dorsal subpial plus central canal enhancement; on sagittal images the same finding appears as a long linear dorsal strip with central canal enhancement. Image the thoracic spine as well, since hilar nodes may be visible.
pos: A trident pattern strongly suggests spinal cord sarcoidosis, even when the lesion is long and could be mistaken for AQP4 or MOG myelitis. It does not replace a tissue diagnosis, so search for a biopsy site with chest CT or whole-body PET-CT. Its absence does not exclude sarcoid because lesions may also show ventral or braid-like enhancement or none.
aN: spinal cord sarcoidosis | trident sign | dorsal subpial and central canal enhancement | three pronged cord enhancement | sarcoid cord trident

det.mechanism: Sarcoid granulomas spread along the leptomeninges and perivascular spaces and enter the cord from its surface, leading to enhancement of the dorsal pia and subpial parenchyma. Spread along the central canal produces the third prong, and the lesion may arise next to spondylotic levels where the blood–cord barrier is already compromised.
det.technique: After a long T2 lesion is found, request thin axial and sagittal post-gadolinium T1 sequences through it. Look for the dorsal strip continuing over two or more segments plus a central dot. Whole-spine imaging may show hilar nodes or cauda equina nodules.
det.interpretation: A trident is a hallmark of sarcoid myelopathy and helps separate it from AQP4 and MOG myelitis, which have different enhancement patterns. It cannot replace tissue diagnosis; many sarcoid cords show other patterns. Its presence should trigger PET-CT and biopsy planning.
pearls: Dorsal subpial strip + central canal dot on axial images = trident.
In sarcoid myelopathy the scan can look dramatic while the patient is only mildly affected.
Always look for hilar nodes on the thoracic spine MRI.
det.thd: Trident sign คือภาพ enhance รูปสามง่ามที่ด้านหลังและกลางของไขสันหลังในการตัดขวางหลังฉีดสารทึบแสง พบจำเพาะใน sarcoid myelopathy ควรตรวจ PET-CT และตัดชิ้นเนื้อยืนยัน

name: H-Sign (MOGAD Myelitis)
formal: Axial T2-weighted MRI pattern in which the spinal cord lesion is confined mainly to the central grey matter, producing an H-shaped hyperintensity; characteristic of MOG antibody-associated myelitis, with frequent conus involvement and often faint, short or longitudinally extensive lesions.
simple: On a cross-section MRI of the spinal cord, the bright area is shaped like the letter H because the inflammation sits in the grey matter. It is a clue to MOG antibody disease.
th: ภาพ MRI ตัดขวางไขสันหลังที่รอยโรค T2 สูงอยู่ที่ central grey matter เป็นรูปตัว H บ่งชี้ myelitis จาก MOGAD และมักพบที่ conus medullaris ได้บ่อย
exam: Review axial T2 images through the lesion, not only sagittal views. Look for a symmetrical H-shaped grey matter hyperintensity, fainter signal than in AQP4 myelitis, possible conus involvement and about half enhancing. Pair it with MOG IgG by live cell-based assay.
pos: An H-sign makes MOGAD myelitis more likely than AQP4-NMOSD or MS and prompts MOG testing and conus imaging. It is not specific, since other grey-matter myelopathies such as viral myelitis, anterior horn disease and ischaemia can look similar, so combine it with antibody testing and clinical context. Absence of the sign does not exclude MOGAD.
aN: mogad myelitis | h sign | h shaped cord lesion | central grey matter sign | grey matter cord lesion mogad | conus medullaris lesion in mogad

det.mechanism: MOG antibodies cause inflammation that mainly affects grey matter and the central cord, unlike AQP4 myelitis, which tends to involve the entire cross-section. Grey matter lesions render an H-shaped signal on axial T2 images, and the conus is frequently affected.
det.technique: Scroll through the axial T2 series across the abnormal segment, not just the sagittal views. Look for a faint symmetrical H shape and examine the conus with dedicated lumbar sequences. Pair imaging with MOG IgG measured by a live cell-based assay.
det.interpretation: An H-sign favours MOGAD over MS and AQP4-NMOSD. Short lesions and conus involvement often coexist with longer lesions. The sign is not unique, because viral myelitis, ischaemia and anterior horn diseases can also involve grey matter.
pearls: H-shaped grey matter hyperintensity plus conus involvement = think MOGAD.
Look at the axial images, not only the sagittal.
Only roughly 50% of MOGAD cord lesions take up contrast.
det.thd: H-sign คือรอยโรค T2 สูงใน central grey matter ของไขสันหลังรูปตัว H ในภาพตัดขวาง พบบ่อยใน myelitis ของ MOGAD ซึ่งมักมี conus เกี่ยวข้อง ควรตรวจ MOG IgG ด้วย cell-based assay

name: Extreme Delta Brush (EEG)
formal: EEG pattern of continuous rhythmic delta activity (roughly 1–3 Hz) carrying superimposed fast beta bursts (roughly 20–30 Hz) on each wave, seen in about 33% of people with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis and described rarely in other autoimmune and non-immune encephalopathies.
simple: A special brain-wave recording pattern in which slow waves carry little bursts of fast activity, like the bristles of a brush. It suggests anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
th: รูปแบบ EEG ที่เป็นคลื่นช้าเดลต้าต่อเนื่องร่วมกับคลื่น beta ความถี่สูงซ้อนอยู่บนแต่ละคลื่น พบประมาณหนึ่งในสามของผู้ป่วย anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis และเกี่ยวกับความรุนแรงของโรค
exam: Request continuous or prolonged EEG in any patient with suspected autoimmune encephalitis and ask the neurophysiologist to look specifically for rhythmic delta with superimposed fast activity. Test NMDAR IgG in CSF and serum whether or not the pattern is seen.
pos: Extreme delta brush strongly supports NMDA receptor encephalitis in the right clinical setting and is associated with a more prolonged illness. It is absent in most patients, and it has been described in other encephalopathies, including some with other antibodies, so it cannot confirm the diagnosis. Generalised slowing, found in about nine in ten patients, is far commoner.
aN: eeg | extreme delta brush | edb | delta brush pattern | nmdar encephalitis eeg pattern

det.mechanism: The pattern is thought to reflect disrupted thalamocortical and cortical oscillations when NMDA receptors are internalised, producing fast beta rhythms riding on slow delta waves. It tends to appear in severe disease and often persists for weeks.
det.technique: Request prolonged EEG (preferably continuous) in suspected autoimmune encephalitis, as the pattern may be intermittent. Ask the neurophysiologist to describe delta activity with superimposed beta bursts rather than just generalised slowing.
det.interpretation: Seen in about one third of NMDAR encephalitis, it strongly supports the diagnosis in the right setting but does not confirm it; rare cases of other autoimmune and non-immune encephalopathies exist. Generalised slowing is much more common and non-specific.
pearls: Delta waves with fast beta 'bristles' = extreme delta brush.
Present in only about one third; absence does not exclude NMDAR encephalitis.
Send NMDAR IgG in CSF and serum regardless.
det.thd: Extreme delta brush คือ EEG ที่มีคลื่นช้า delta ต่อเนื่องและมีคลื่น beta ความถี่สูงซ้อนบนทุกคลื่น พบประมาณหนึ่งในสามของ NMDAR encephalitis ช่วยสนับสนุนการวินิจฉัยแต่ไม่ยืนยัน

name: Jaw-Closing Dystonia with Laryngospasm
formal: Episodic involuntary clenching of the jaw, sometimes with a stridulous inspiratory sound from laryngeal closure, reported in anti-Ri (ANNA-2) brainstem encephalitis; considered highly characteristic and may be so severe that feeding is compromised or a tracheostomy is needed.
simple: Sudden episodes in which the jaw locks shut and the throat tightens, making breathing noisy. When seen in an older woman with unsteadiness, it points to a cancer-related immune attack on the brainstem (anti-Ri).
th: อาการขากรรไกรเกร็งปิดเป็นช่วง ๆ ร่วมกับ laryngospasm และเสียงหายใจเข้าดังหวีด พบใน brainstem encephalitis จาก anti-Ri (ANNA-2) สัมพันธ์กับมะเร็งเต้านมหรือปอด อาจรุนแรงจนต้องเจาะคอ
exam: Observe or video the episodes, noting triggers, duration, stridor and oxygen saturation; examine the temporomandibular joint and teeth for trauma and test mouth opening between episodes. Look for opsoclonus, ataxia and myoclonus, and ensure airway safety.
pos: Recurrent jaw-closing dystonia with laryngospasm strongly suggests anti-Ri paraneoplastic encephalitis, prompting antibody testing and a search for breast or small cell lung cancer. It is distinct from tetanus (persistent trismus after a wound), drug-induced dystonia and bruxism, none of which cause episodic laryngeal closure.
aN: jaw closing dystonia | jaw clenching episodes | trismus with laryngospasm | anti ri jaw dystonia | anna 2 jaw spasm

det.mechanism: Anti-Ri encephalitis damages brainstem nuclei and circuits that control jaw and laryngeal muscles, producing paroxysmal sustained contraction of the masseters and laryngeal adductors. The autoimmune target is the NOVA family of RNA-binding proteins in brainstem and cerebellar neurons.
det.technique: Record the episodes on video, noting duration, triggers (swallowing, speaking, startle), stridor and oxygen saturation, and examine jaw opening, dentition and swallowing between episodes. Look for coexisting opsoclonus, myoclonus and ataxia.
det.interpretation: Considered highly characteristic of anti-Ri brainstem encephalitis, particularly in women whose tumour is a breast or lung carcinoma. Tetanus, drug-induced dystonia, bruxism, functional spasm and oromandibular dystonia should be distinguished.
pearls: Jaw clamping + stridor + ataxia in an older woman: test anti-Ri and screen the breast.
Airway protection takes priority; some patients need a tracheostomy.
Botulinum toxin or benzodiazepines can relieve jaw spasm while immunotherapy takes effect.
det.thd: Jaw-closing dystonia with laryngospasm คืออาการขากรรไกรเกร็งปิดเป็นช่วงร่วมกับเสียงหายใจดัง พบใน anti-Ri brainstem encephalitis ควรตรวจหามะเร็งเต้านมหรือปอดและดูแลทางเดินหายใจ

name: Downbeat Nystagmus
formal: Vertical nystagmus with the slow phase directed upward and the fast phase downward in primary gaze, usually increasing on lateral and downward gaze; indicates dysfunction of the cerebellar flocculus or craniocervical junction and is a recognised sign of GAD65 antibody and paraneoplastic cerebellar disease.
simple: Eyes drift up slowly and flick down quickly, so the world seems to jump vertically. It points to a problem in the cerebellum or the junction of skull and neck.
th: ตากระตุกลงในแนวตั้ง โดยลูกตาลอยขึ้นช้า ๆ แล้วกระตุกกลับลงเร็ว ผู้ป่วยรู้สึกภาพกระโดดขึ้นลง บ่งชี้ความผิดปกติที่ cerebellum (flocculus) หรือ craniocervical junction และพบได้ใน GAD65 cerebellar ataxia
exam: Examine in primary gaze with fixation (and with fixation removed), then in lateral and downward gaze and with the head turned or tilted; ask about oscillopsia. Look for saccadic intrusions, impaired smooth pursuit and gaze-holding. Consider the Dix-Hallpike manoeuvre to rule out positional vertigo.
pos: Persistent downbeat nystagmus localises to the cerebellum or craniocervical junction. Causes include Chiari malformation, cerebellar degeneration, drugs (antiepileptics, lithium), vitamin B1 or magnesium deficiency, stroke, multiple sclerosis and autoimmune cerebellar disease such as GAD65 antibodies. A negative MRI should lead to antibody testing and drug and metabolic review.
aN: down beat nystagmus | vertical nystagmus downbeating | cerebellar vertical nystagmus | dbn

det.mechanism: Downbeat nystagmus arises from asymmetric vertical vestibulo-ocular drive, usually from dysfunction of the cerebellar flocculus and paraflocculus, which normally inhibit the anterior canal pathways. Lesions at the craniocervical junction or in the vestibulocerebellum release upward slow-phase drift followed by a corrective downward saccade.
det.technique: Test in primary gaze with and without fixation, then in lateral and down-gaze, and with head tilt or hyperventilation. Ask about oscillopsia, and look for other cerebellar signs and saccadic intrusions. Check positional manoeuvres to rule out benign positional vertigo.
det.interpretation: It localises to the cerebellum or craniocervical junction. Common causes are cerebellar degeneration, Chiari malformation, drug or metabolic effects, stroke and MS, and autoimmune causes include GAD65 and paraneoplastic antibodies. MRI of the craniocervical junction and a drug and electrolyte review come first.
pearls: Always image the craniocervical junction in downbeat nystagmus.
Isolated downbeat nystagmus can be a GAD65 manifestation: send the antibody.
4-aminopyridine or 3,4-diaminopyridine may reduce oscillopsia in selected patients.
det.thd: Downbeat nystagmus คือตากระตุกลงในแนวตั้ง บ่งชี้ปัญหาที่ cerebellum หรือ craniocervical junction ควรทำ MRI บริเวณนั้นและตรวจ GAD65 antibody เมื่อไม่พบสาเหตุโครงสร้าง

name: CHIT1-Positive Giant Cells (Muscle Biopsy)
formal: Multinucleated giant cells within muscle granulomas that stain for chitinase 1 (chitotriosidase, CHIT1) and for CD68; the stain identifies true histiocytic giant cells of granulomatous myositis (sarcoid) and is negative in pure inclusion body myositis.
simple: A special stain on the muscle biopsy that lights up the big fused immune cells of a granuloma. If it is positive, the biopsy shows true granulomatous myositis such as sarcoid, not just inclusion body myositis.
ab: giant cell marker in sarcoid myopathy
th: การย้อม CHIT1 บนชิ้นเนื้อกล้ามเนื้อ ติดสีที่ multinucleated giant cell ใน granuloma ช่วยยืนยันว่าเป็น giant cell ของ granulomatous myositis เช่น sarcoid และให้ผลลบใน IBM แท้
exam: Not a bedside sign: ask the neuropathologist to add CHIT1 (with CD68) immunohistochemistry on frozen sections of a muscle with granulomas, and to cut step sections because granulomas can be focal. Interpret together with HLA class I and II staining and with IBM markers (rimmed vacuoles, COX-negative fibres, p62).
pos: CHIT1-positive giant cells confirm histiocytic granulomatous myositis, as in sarcoid myopathy and SaM-IBM, and help to distinguish true giant cells from regenerating myogenic multinucleated fibres. Negative staining in a biopsy with IBM features supports pure IBM. The stain does not tell SaM from SaM-IBM and is not validated in other causes such as tuberculosis, so infection must still be excluded.
nN: chit1 positive giant cells muscle biopsy
aN: muscle biopsy | chit1 positive giant cells | chitinase 1 giant cells | chitotriosidase staining | chit1 immunostain | giant cell marker in sarcoid myopathy

det.mechanism: Chitinase 1 is secreted by activated, mature macrophages and is a known blood and tissue marker of activity in pulmonary sarcoidosis. In sarcoid muscle the enzyme is concentrated in the fused giant cells of the granuloma, while single macrophages and monocytes stay unstained. Pure inclusion body myositis has macrophages that invade fibres but do not fuse into giant cells and lack CHIT1.
det.technique: Request CHIT1 together with CD68 on a frozen section, alongside the standard panel of HLA class I and II, CD4, CD8, p62 and COX/SDH. Granulomas can be sparse, so ask for step sections through the block. Compare staining with the H&E slide to ensure that stained cells are truly multinucleated histiocytes.
det.interpretation: Positive giant cells indicate true granulomatous myositis, most often sarcoid, and they separate it from IBM, in which CHIT1 is absent. It cannot distinguish sarcoid myopathy from the SaM-IBM overlap, so IBM markers must still be sought. It is a research-derived stain with limited availability, and it does not replace culture and special stains for tuberculosis and fungi.
pearls: CHIT1 positive = histiocytic giant cells; negative CHIT1 in a vacuolated biopsy favours pure IBM.
Ask for step sections as well as the stain: granulomas can be patchy.
Still stain and culture for AFB and fungi before attributing granulomas to sarcoid.
det.thd: CHIT1 คือเอนไซม์ chitinase 1 ที่ติดสีเฉพาะที่ multinucleated giant cell ใน granuloma ของกล้ามเนื้อ ช่วยแยก granulomatous myositis เช่น sarcoid ออกจาก IBM แท้ซึ่งไม่ติดสี แต่แยก SaM กับ SaM-IBM ไม่ได้ ควรขอ step sections และต้องตรวจเชื้อวัณโรคและเชื้อรา

name: Livedo Racemosa
formal: Fixed, broken (irregular, branching) violaceous net-like skin discolouration that does not fade on warming, usually on the limbs and trunk, due to impaired cutaneous arterial flow; seen in polyarteritis nodosa, cutaneous arteritis, ADA2 deficiency, Sneddon syndrome and antiphospholipid syndrome.
simple: A lace-like purple pattern on the skin with gaps and broken lines. Unlike the fine, regular mottling of cold skin (livedo reticularis), it stays when the skin is warm and signals a blood vessel problem that can also affect nerves or the brain.
th: ผื่นลายร่างแหสีม่วงแบบไม่ต่อเนื่อง กิ่งก้านไม่สม่ำเสมอ ไม่จางลงเมื่อทำให้ผิวอุ่น พบในโรคหลอดเลือดแดงอักเสบ เช่น PAN, ADA2 deficiency, Sneddon’s syndrome และ antiphospholipid syndrome บ่งถึงปัญหาที่หลอดเลือดแดงของผิวหนัง และอาจสัมพันธ์กับเส้นประสาทอักเสบหรือ stroke
exam: Inspect the thighs, legs, buttocks and arms in good light after warming the skin or limb for several minutes. A fixed, irregular, open-ringed network with broken branches that persists is livedo racemosa; a complete symmetrical fine net that fades with warmth is physiological livedo reticularis. Photograph and map the lesion, and palpate for tender nodules or ulcers.
pos: Persistent livedo racemosa should lead to a search for vasculitis and thrombotic vasculopathy: it is common in cutaneous PAN and in DADA2, and in Sneddon syndrome where it accompanies recurrent stroke. Combine it with blood pressure, urinalysis, ANCA, antiphospholipid antibodies, ADA2 activity when young, and a deep biopsy that reaches the subcutis. It is not specific and can occur with other disorders such as cholesterol emboli.
aN: livedo racemosa | broken livedo | branching livedo | livedo reticularis vasculitic | fixed livedo | net like cyanotic skin pattern

det.mechanism: Cutaneous arteries feeding the skin lobules narrow or occlude through inflammation, thrombosis or endothelial proliferation, so the capillary network fills with deoxygenated blood in a segmentally interrupted pattern. When the supplying arteriolar cones are completely blocked, the net is broken and does not recede with warmth, unlike the fully reversible vasomotor mottling of cold exposure.
det.technique: Warm the patient and examine the whole skin surface in strong light, noting symmetry, ring completeness and colour. Mark lesions, photograph them for serial comparison and palpate for nodules. Biopsy a nodule or the centre of a violaceous ring down to fat rather than a superficial punch.
det.interpretation: Persistent broken livedo implies arterial disease, such as PAN, cutaneous arteritis, DADA2, antiphospholipid syndrome, cholesterol emboli or Sneddon syndrome. Fine regular livedo reticularis that fades on warming is usually benign. Neurologists should ask about stroke, mononeuritis multiplex and hypertension in patients showing the broken pattern.
pearls: Broken and warm-resistant = racemosa; complete and fading = reticularis.
Livedo racemosa plus recurrent stroke in a young adult: test antiphospholipid antibodies and consider Sneddon or DADA2.
Biopsy deep to fat to reach the medium-sized artery.
det.thd: Livedo racemosa คือผื่นลายร่างแหสีม่วงที่เป็นวงไม่ครบและไม่จางเมื่อทำให้อุ่น แตกต่างจาก livedo reticularis ที่เป็นร่างแหละเอียดสม่ำเสมอและหายเมื่อผิวอุ่นขึ้น มักบ่งถึงหลอดเลือดแดงของผิวหนังอุดตันหรืออักเสบ เช่น PAN, DADA2, Sneddon’s syndrome และ antiphospholipid syndrome ควรตัดชิ้นเนื้อให้ลึกถึงไขมันและตรวจหาโรคในอวัยวะอื่นร่วมด้วย

name: Temporal Artery Halo Sign (Ultrasound)
formal: Homogeneous, hypoechoic, circumferential thickening of the arterial wall seen around a compressible lumen on colour Doppler ultrasound in both longitudinal and transverse planes; the characteristic sonographic sign of giant-cell arteritis in temporal and axillary arteries.
simple: On an ultrasound scan of the temple (or armpit) artery, the artery wall looks like a dark ring around the blood flow, like a halo. It suggests inflamed, swollen arteries from giant-cell arteritis.
th: เห็นผนังหลอดเลือดแดงหนาตัวเป็นวงสีเข้ม (hypoechoic) รอบ lumen ใน ultrasound ทั้งแนวยาวและแนวขวาง เกิดจากผนังบวมอักเสบ เป็นลักษณะจำเพาะของ giant-cell arteritis ที่ temporal และ axillary artery ยิ่งพบหลายตำแหน่งยิ่งมีโอกาสสัมพันธ์กับ ischaemic optic neuropathy
exam: Not a bedside sign: a trained operator scans the common superficial temporal artery and its frontal and parietal branches, and the axillary arteries, with a high-frequency linear probe and gentle pressure. Persistent wall thickening visible in two planes that does not compress away is positive; counting involved segments (halo count) and grading thickness (halo score) adds weight.
pos: A convincing halo in an older patient with a compatible syndrome supports urgent glucocorticoid treatment and, in many centres, can replace biopsy. In a prospective study the sign was about as sensitive as biopsy and slightly less specific, but results depend on operator skill and steroids shorten its visibility. False positives include atherosclerosis, myeloma, lymphoma and other vasculitides; multiple positive segments predict ischaemic optic neuropathy.
aN: ultrasound | temporal artery halo sign | halo sign | temporal artery halo | compression sign | halo count | halo score | vessel wall edema sign

det.mechanism: Inflammatory oedema and mural thickening make the artery wall hypoechoic, while the lumen remains dark with colour flow. The thickening is concentric, reflecting intimal and medial infiltration with swelling, and it shrinks over days to weeks of steroid treatment.
det.technique: Use a high-frequency linear probe (preferably 15 MHz or higher), scan the common trunk and both branches in two planes with minimal pressure, and add the axillary arteries. Look for compressibility and persistence in two planes, record the number of involved segments and measure wall thickness; scan early because steroid therapy gradually removes the sign.
det.interpretation: A halo in several segments, supported by compatible symptoms and raised inflammatory markers, strongly supports giant-cell arteritis and correlates with biopsy positivity and ischaemic optic neuropathy. The sensitivity ranged from about two thirds to above 90% across studies and depends on the examiner. Atherosclerotic plaque, lymphoma, myeloma or other vasculitis may mimic it, and a negative scan does not exclude GCA if the story is convincing.
pearls: Scan before or within days of starting steroids.
Include the axillary arteries.
Multiple halo segments predict visual involvement.
det.thd: Halo sign คือผนังหลอดเลือดแดง temporal ที่หนาตัวเป็นวงสีเข้มรอบ lumen ใน ultrasound ทั้งแนวยาวและแนวขวาง เกิดจากผนังอักเสบบวม พบใน giant-cell arteritis ควรตรวจก่อนหรือภายในไม่กี่วันหลังเริ่มสเตียรอยด์ และตรวจ axillary artery ร่วมด้วย ผลลบไม่ตัดโรคออกถ้าอาการเข้าได้ชัดเจน และต้องเริ่มรักษาโดยไม่รอผล

name: Pallid Optic Disc Swelling
formal: Chalky-white, oedematous optic nerve head (often with cotton-wool spots and a small cup) seen on fundoscopy in arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy, reflecting infarction of the optic nerve head from posterior ciliary artery occlusion in giant-cell arteritis.
simple: The front of the optic nerve looks swollen and pale white rather than the usual pink-red swollen disc. In an older person with sudden vision loss, it is a warning sign of giant-cell arteritis.
th: จานประสาทตา (optic disc) บวมและซีดขาวแบบชอล์ก มักพบ cotton-wool spots ร่วม เป็นลักษณะของ arteritic anterior ischaemic optic neuropathy จาก giant-cell arteritis ซึ่งหลอดเลือด posterior ciliary ถูกอุดตัน ต่างจาก NAION ที่จานประสาทตามักบวมสีแดงชมพู
exam: Dilate the pupil and examine the disc for colour and swelling in the setting of sudden monocular visual loss and a relative afferent pupillary defect. A disc that is pale and chalky, perhaps with cotton-wool spots or a normal-sized cup, favours arteritic over non-arteritic disease; check for temporal artery tenderness, jaw claudication and take ESR/CRP the same day.
pos: Pallid swelling points to arteritic AION and should prompt immediate steroids and urgent GCA work-up, because the second eye can be lost within days. Hyperaemic swelling with a crowded disc suggests NAION, but the distinction is not absolute, so fluorescein angiography or OCT angiography can help when the picture is uncertain.
aN: pallid disc edema | pale swollen optic disc | chalky white disc swelling | arteritic aion disc | pallid edema

det.mechanism: In giant-cell arteritis, inflamed posterior ciliary arteries become occluded, causing infarction of the optic nerve head. The infarcted tissue is oedematous and loses its pink perfusion, producing a chalky appearance, often with associated choroidal ischaemia.
det.technique: Examine the dilated fundus for disc colour, oedema, haemorrhages, cotton-wool spots and cup size, compare both eyes, and check visual acuity, colour vision and the relative afferent pupillary defect. Combine with the rest of the neuro-ophthalmological exam and same-day ESR, CRP and platelet count.
det.interpretation: A pallid swollen disc in a patient aged 50 or more is arteritic AION until proved otherwise, and requires immediate treatment. A hyperaemic, crowded disc is more typical of NAION. Visual loss is usually severe and the fellow eye is at risk within days if untreated, so do not wait for the biopsy.
pearls: Pale and chalky means think GCA; pink and crowded means think NAION.
Visual loss in GCA is an emergency: give steroids first.
Examine the second eye too, since fellow-eye involvement can follow quickly.
